Dataset We choose the DuRecDial 2.0 (Liu et al., 2021) dataset as appropriate for our experiments, which is a crowdsourced dataset of human-to-human dialogues in recommendation-oriented scenarios. The significant reason for using DuRecDial is that this dataset contains rich auxiliary information, such as movies or celebrities that users like, and even food preferences. This information can assist LLM in generating high-quality plans. In fact, we conducted comprehensive experiments on the ReDial dataset (Li et al., 2019), but due to the lack of auxiliary information, the results were not as expected. Another reason is the scarcity of manually constructed high-quality datasets in the target-driven dialogue domain, but our method

provides a solution to address this issue. Additionally, we conducted evaluation experiments using the TGConv (Yang et al., 2022) dataset for multi-turn self-play simulations. The TGConv dataset contains high-quality open-domain dialogues on a variety of commonsense topics. Each dialogue is designed to direct the conversation towards a specific keyword or topic through coherent keyword transitions, which are categorized as either easy-to-reach or hard-to-reach based on their difficulty level.

Baselines For conversation generation, our baselines include: GPT-2 (Radford et al., 2019), DialogGPT (Zhang et al., 2020), BART (Lewis et al., 2020), TCP-Dial (Wang et al., 2022), COLOR (Wang et al., 2023a), and TopKG (Yang et al., 2022). We choose these methods because they are highly relevant to our problem setting, and COLOR is currently the state-of-the-art model in our knowledge. In addition to guiding ChatGPT to generate conversations, we also conduct experiments on DialogGPT to make a fair comparison.

Evaluation Metrics Inspired by (Wang et al., 2023a), we adopt the same evaluation metrics, including perplexity (PPL), distinct (D-1/2) (Li et al., 2016), BLEU-n (B-1/2) (Papineni et al., 2002), wordlevel F1 and knowledge F1 (Know. F1) (Liu et al., 2020). To evaluate models' goal-directed performance, we use the goal success rate (Succ.) as the global evaluation metric. In DuRecDial 2.0 dataset, Succ. measures the proportion of correct target topic generation within the target turn and the two adjacent turns in the test set, as per Wang et al. (2023a). Additionally, we also use Coherence (Section 4.2) as another global evaluation metric, which measures the average contextual semantic similarity between the last utterance in the context and generated utterances.
